Done! Your `.env` file will now load automatically in every PowerShell session. Here's what I set up:

**PowerShell Profile** (`/home/author\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\profile.ps1`):
- Automatically loads your project's `.env` file every time PowerShell starts
- Also loads any `.env` file from the current directory (useful if you have multiple projects)
- Provides a `Load-EnvFile` function you can call manually if needed

The next time you open PowerShell, your environment variables (`API_BASE_URL`, `API_KEY`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `NPM_TOKEN`) will be automatically available.

**To verify it's working**, open a new PowerShell terminal and run:
```powershell
echo $env:API_KEY
```

If you see your API key, it's working! If you need to reload manually in an existing session, you can call `Load-EnvFile ".\.env"` or `Load-EnvFile $ProjectEnv`.
